newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: HK Bank sees no fund exodus from Philippines.
newsitem.headline: HK Bank sees no fund exodus from Philippines.

text.p: There has not been any significant outflow of foreign fund money from the Philippines in the wake of the instability of the peso, the head of Hongkong Bank in the Philippines said on Wednesday.
"We haven't seen any major outflows of portfolio investment which is a good sign for the Philippines," Brian Fredrick told Reuters.
The bank is the biggest custodian of foreign equity investment in the Philippine stock market.
There has been suspicion in the Philippines that foreign investors may have been behind last week's de facto devaluation of the peso, which has fallen close to 12 percent.
"We have not seen it through us," he said.
He said he did not believe there was a conspiracy to drive down the peso, but noted many economists believed that the currency, in terms of purchasing power parity, had been overvalued.
The Philippine stock market has fallen sharply since the peso plunged but analysts said the money had moved into high yielding local fixed income instruments.
Fredrick added that the peso appeared stable at the current level of 29/29.50 to the dollar.
